title: France, Lebanon and Jordan Meet in Paris to Shape UNIFIL Successor Mission
detail: September 17, 2026 — French President Emmanuel Macron hosted Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Jordan's King Abdullah II at the Invalides in Paris, alongside senior European and Arab military and political officials, to discuss international support for the cash-strapped Lebanese Armed Forces and options for a new multinational mission to succeed the UN's UNIFIL peacekeeping force, which is due to withdraw by the end of the year. France and Italy are leading efforts to stand up a training-and-advisory mission, with more than 10 EU states reportedly ready to contribute. Aoun called for 'a long-term partnership' rather than a temporary fix, saying any transition 'must not lead to any security vacuum' and must instead strengthen state authority; Macron said supporting the Lebanese Army is 'crucial' to filling the space left by Israeli forces in the south, while King Abdullah highlighted the Army's need for spare parts and drone-detection equipment. France and Jordan separately signed a bilateral defense cooperation agreement. The summit took place against the backdrop of a fragile June 26 framework: Israel has hardened its position on withdrawal from south Lebanon ahead of its October elections, and the 8th round of US-mediated Rome talks on Hezbollah disarmament — postponed from mid-September — remains pending. The parties agreed to reconvene at year's end to assess progress.

title: Russia Tells OSCE It Will Not Accept a Ukraine Ceasefire Without a 'Root Causes' Settlement
detail: September 17, 2026 — Russia's permanent representative to the OSCE, Dmitry Polyansky, told a closed session of the OSCE Permanent Council in Vienna that Moscow 'will never agree to a ceasefire without reaching a comprehensive understanding of the key parameters of the peace agreements that would eliminate the root causes of the Ukrainian crisis.' Polyansky said Russia's conditions for halting hostilities are well known and unchanged, and that Russia intends to continue its military campaign 'until its goals are fully achieved, either peacefully or militarily,' while also warning that any NATO troop presence in Ukraine would be treated as the alliance's direct participation in the war. The statement reiterates Moscow's longstanding position roughly a week after Witkoff and Kushner's first-ever Kyiv visit and a Trump-Putin call (Sep 8) that ended without a ceasefire, and underscores why Ukraine remains outside the tracker's in-force ceasefire count.

title: DRC-Rwanda 7th JSCM Session Ends in Geneva Without a Joint Communiqué
detail: September 17, 2026 — The two-day seventh session of the DRC-Rwanda Joint Security Coordination Mechanism (JSCM) concluded in Geneva with US, Qatari, Togolese and African Union Commission mediators present, but — unlike the detailed joint statement issued after the sixth JSCM meeting in mid-August — the parties did not release a joint communiqué setting out new agreements or implementation deadlines. Discussions covered FDLR neutralization commitments, Rwanda's defensive-measure disengagement, monitoring and verification of the June 2025 Washington Accords, and the DRC's disarmament-demobilization-reintegration (DDR) plan for FDLR forces, including consultations with MONUSCO on prior DDR experience. The two sides remain divided over how 'neutralization' is defined. An October 2026 trilateral planning conference is scheduled to produce a revised Operations Order for coordinated implementation.
